biography.plain_text: Vittorio Malacalza is a Genoa-based Italian industrialist who built his fortune in steel. After inheriting his father’s construction company and leaving engineering studies, he progressed from motorway contracting to industrial components, then established a European steel business. Its sale supplied the capital for the Malacalza family’s later industrial, property and financial investments.

long_biography.plain_text:
Rebuilding Trametal and Spartan UK made Vittorio Malacalza a major figure in European steel plate. He developed the businesses with his sons, combining production in Italy and Britain with steel trading and international partnerships. By the time the mills changed hands, they had grown into a significant continental operator.

Malacalza also placed advanced engineering alongside steel. The family acquired Ansaldo’s superconducting-magnet unit and developed it as ASG Superconductors, which supplied magnets for CERN’s Large Hadron Collider and fusion projects including ITER. Its applications expanded to superconducting cables for energy transmission and open magnetic-resonance systems for medical imaging.
